catalysts: Next Canadian labor and CPI prints that keep slack visible versus core near 2%.
BoC communications that refuse to validate a 100bp-plus hiking path after the energy-pass-through minutes.
Softening energy impulse if the Saudi/Oman crude workaround continues to cap the supply tail.
Further evidence that housing/FCI channels are biting (AU housing analog; CA consumer 45).

context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether Canadian domestic demand (labor 38, consumer 45, core near 2%) can validate a BoC hiking cycle of about 122bp by Sep 2027. Mechanism: imported energy and a just-delivered Fed hike have been used to price a catch-up tightening path; if the labor/consumption channel is already slack, that path is a policy-error/overtightening price that should unwind as realized CA data refuse to confirm pass-through. Transmission is fewer delivered hikes and a lower CRAU27 implied rate, not a required CAD spot crash.

Paper books are empty $100m seeds, so there is no legacy perma-bear inventory. Cannot reject a flow-only explanation; cannot confirm one either. Treat ownership as unknown and keep size modest.

analogs: CA-US_2Y analog 2024-12-18: prior 1m move -17bp, level -130bp versus today's -140bp; subsequent 1m -3bp and 3m -20bp, so the spread stayed or went more negative as US restriction outran Canada.
CA-US_2Y analog 2025-01-30: prior 1m -17bp, level -145bp, nearly identical to today's -140bp; subsequent 1m -5bp then 3m +25bp, a later partial mean-reversion once the growth/policy impulse faded.
CA-US_2Y analog 2024-05-02: prior 1m -17bp, level -63bp; subsequent 1m -9bp and 3m -6bp. Directionally similar near-term follow-through, at a much less extreme level than today.

historical_reference.distribution: CA 2Y 3.27 is 97.8th percentile of 1y (z 2.46) but only 58.6th percentile of 5y, so the stretch is a one-year re-pricing not a five-year extreme. CRAU27 +122bp from overnight is a large policy-path gap relative to a 2.29 benchmark. These percentiles are discovery flags, not the thesis.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Unlike 2023-03 banking-stress hike-path unwinds, this packet has no documented CA banking shock. Unlike 2022 energy-spike hiking, CA core is near 2% and the inflation gauge is only 55; the hawkish residual is energy pass-through and Fed spillover, not a domestic overheat. US gauges remain hot (labor 75, inflation 72, activity 69, consumer 74), so this is a Canada-specific demand/policy-path discrepancy, not a synchronized G10 recession print. Temperature gauges are repo-retained dashboard_v8 and may be stale versus live Supabase scores.

independent_checks: Policy-path versus overnight: CORRA 2.29 versus CRAU27 3.51 (+122bp) and a 2028 peak of 3.655, a fully specified MX CRA hiking cycle.
Demand versus inflation gauges: CA labor 38 and consumer 45 versus inflation 55 and activity 66; hard CPI holds at 3% with core near 2%.
Cross-market: CA-US 2Y already -140bp (near 1y/5y lows) while US SOFR path still rises to SR3U7 4.755; Canada is being asked to catch a hotter US cycle it is not running.

Peer tightening channel: AU housing downturn under higher rates with AONIA still pricing about 60bp of hikes (peak 4.945 versus AONIA 4.35) shows the same late-cycle FCI bite the BoC path would intensify.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: Fed hike bias, August US CPI keeping that bias intact, CA August CPI at 3% with core near 2%, BoC energy-pass-through minutes, and AU housing already weakening under higher rates. Marginal now: the live CORRA 2027 strip still embeds a full hiking cycle after those facts; SOFR 3.85 is a realized FCI impulse; Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail even as a separate rollup says energy shock absorbers are weakening. Labor 38 is a state, not a new print in this packet; what is new is using that known slack against a still-hawkish 2027 CORRA path.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that Canada can or should deliver that 122bp path. Core near 2% and labor 38 imply the energy/Fed impulse is being over-weighted; the priced hike cycle is the fragile assumption.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: CRAU27 at 3.51 versus CORRA 2.29 requires the BoC to deliver roughly 122bp of tightening by Sep 2027, i.e. a multi-hike catch-up toward US restriction, justified by energy pass-through rather than by current core inflation or labor tightness.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Overnight CORRA is 2.29 as of 2026-09-17. The 3m strip then prices Dec-26 2.775 (+48.5bp), Mar-27 3.13 (+84bp), Jun-27 3.365 (+107.5bp), Sep-27 3.51 (+122bp), and a 2028 peak near 3.655. CA 2Y is already 3.27 (97.8th percentile of 1y, z 2.46) and CA 2s10s has flattened 18bp over 1m to 56bp (0.6th percentile of 1y). CA-US 2Y is -140bp (3.8th percentile of 1y, -17bp over 1m). That path was built after the Sep-16 FOMC (futures had >90% odds of a 25bp hike, subsequently delivered to 3.75-4.00%) and after BoC minutes flagged energy pass-through, while official SOFR jumped to 3.85 on 2026-09-17 from 3.62 the prior day.

holes_in_opposing_case: value-guy and carry-is-king short CA-US_2Y as if a 3.8th/4.3rd percentile is a closing mechanism for higher CA rates. That percentile is a discovery flag. Their own packet analogs split: 2025-01-30 later mean-reverted (+25bp 3m) while 2024-12-18 stayed/went more negative (-20bp 3m). Convergence via CA rates up requires the BoC to deliver the 84-122bp CRA path that labor 38 and core near 2% do not validate. Overnight CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 is a level gap, not evidence Canada will catch the hotter US cycle.

carry-is-king frames paying CA 2Y / receiving US 2Y as 'patient carry' after a delivered Fed hike. The 149bp 2Y gap is the invitation to fade Canada cheapness only if CORRA catch-up is the base case. Dec 1m CORRA at 2.58 still prices almost no near-term hike; the 122bp is loaded into 2027. That is the overpriced object, not a holding-period engine.

dollar-king long USDCAD correctly notes EURUSD/USDCHF already did more USD work and that CA labor/core are soft, then tags ca_rates_view higher. Those two claims fight. If Canada cannot hike, the policy-gap story is receive CORRA, not assume CRA catch-up caps the pair from the Canada side. Energy (BoC minutes versus the Saudi/Oman crude workaround) can hold CAD even if CRAU27 fails to deliver, which is why USDCAD was rejected as the expression.

perma-bull long NZDUSD treats a 0.2% q/q GDP print that beat forecasts as falsifying labor 32 / consumer 38. The print is still a slowdown. An India FTA covering ~95% of NZ exports is not a 4-12 week demand impulse that rewrites slack. NZ rates are unavailable, so the seat cannot show the cheap NZD is inconsistent with the NZ policy path. US gauges remain 69-75 after a delivered hike; that is not a risk-on USD-down regime.

cross-merchant short AUDNZD / NZD higher uses the 5y AUDNZD extreme as if NZ is the strong leg. The 16 Sep tape is AU housing contraction plus an NZ slowdown-that-beat. Inflation gauges are both hot (AU 82, NZ 80) while NZ labor is 32. Bidding NZD in the cross needs NZ rates or a growth-state change the packet does not mark.

rate-hawk and trend-follower pay SOFR_2027-09 on US heat 72/75/69/74 and a 90.5bp remaining SR3 path. That US-rates-up view is compatible with this seat. Their CA_RATES_UP / CAD_DOWN package is not: importing the Fed waypoint into a 122bp BoC cycle is the policy-error price CRAU27 already embeds. US restriction can persist without Canada delivering catch-up.

rate-dove receives CORRA_2027-06 on the same labor/core versus hike-path gap, then claims carry supports the trade. Fading a path that still prices 107.5bp to Jun-27 and 136.5bp to 2028-09 has negative path carry if those hikes print. Direction agrees; the carry claim does not.

mean-reverter's AONIA_2026-10 fade is not the USD/CAD/NZD opposite. The hole is only that AU inflation 82 still fights a 21bp October receive, which is why this seat would not have chosen AONIA as the primary slowdown expression.

attack: Strongest opposing claim: CA-US_2Y at -140bp is 'too cheap' so Canada must hike (value-guy, carry-is-king) or CAD must cheapen while CA rates rise (dollar-king). That closing mechanism is the priced assumption this seat disagrees with. CRAU27 at 3.51 versus CORRA 2.29 already is that hike path. Labor 38, consumer 45, core near 2%, and inflation gauge 55 are the independent checks that the path is too hawkish, not that overnight 2.29 is an unsustainable 2Y anchor that must catch SOFR 3.85.

Second opposing claim: NZD is the cheap cyclical to buy after a GDP beat and FTA (perma-bull, cross-merchant). NZDUSD is already -3.90% 1m at the 12.9th percentile of 1y. A 0.2% q/q slowdown that beat a forecast does not convert labor 32 into a risk-on bid, and NZ policy/2Y cannot be marked. The defensive expression remains NZD lower as a view, not a reason to abandon CORRA duration.

Third: paying SOFR because US heat is real (rate-hawk, trend-follower). Concede the US side. It does not license 122bp of CAD hikes. Spillover is the story that built CRAU27; it is not confirmation the BoC should or will deliver it.
defense: Original trade stands: long duration CORRA_2027-09 / CRAU27. The discrepancy lives in the CAD policy path, not in USDCAD, NZDUSD, AUDNZD, or CA-US_2Y. Packet P&L on rates is inverted, so long duration profits if implied CORRA falls from 3.51. That is unchanged.

USD higher / CAD lower / NZD lower remain directional implications, not the risk. Transmission was already specified as fewer delivered CA hikes, not a required CAD crash. Energy can mix CAD spot; that is why spot was the inferior candidate. FX-view conflicts do not move the rates expression.

What would concede: CRAU27 implied through the packet 2028 peak of 3.655, or CA labor/activity re-accelerating with core well above 2%, or energy pass-through becoming a generalized CPI impulse that the BoC explicitly hikes into. A 4th-percentile CA-US_2Y print, a 0.2% NZ GDP beat, or hotter US gauges alone would not.

Uncertainty preserved: CFTC/CME missing; CORRA OI/volume null; gauges dashboard_v8; CA activity 66 is not recessionary; US heat can import some CA tightening. Confidence stays 58. Seat does not rank opponents or assert a house view.
holes_in_opposing_case: value-guy and carry-is-king short CA-US_2Y as if a 3.8th/4.3rd percentile is a closing mechanism for higher CA rates. That percentile is a discovery flag. Their own packet analogs split: 2025-01-30 later mean-reverted (+25bp 3m) while 2024-12-18 stayed/went more negative (-20bp 3m). Convergence via CA rates up requires the BoC to deliver the 84-122bp CRA path that labor 38 and core near 2% do not validate. Overnight CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 is a level gap, not evidence Canada will catch the hotter US cycle.

carry-is-king frames paying CA 2Y / receiving US 2Y as 'patient carry' after a delivered Fed hike. The 149bp 2Y gap is the invitation to fade Canada cheapness only if CORRA catch-up is the base case. Dec 1m CORRA at 2.58 still prices almost no near-term hike; the 122bp is loaded into 2027. That is the overpriced object, not a holding-period engine.

dollar-king long USDCAD correctly notes EURUSD/USDCHF already did more USD work and that CA labor/core are soft, then tags ca_rates_view higher. Those two claims fight. If Canada cannot hike, the policy-gap story is receive CORRA, not assume CRA catch-up caps the pair from the Canada side. Energy (BoC minutes versus the Saudi/Oman crude workaround) can hold CAD even if CRAU27 fails to deliver, which is why USDCAD was rejected as the expression.

perma-bull long NZDUSD treats a 0.2% q/q GDP print that beat forecasts as falsifying labor 32 / consumer 38. The print is still a slowdown. An India FTA covering ~95% of NZ exports is not a 4-12 week demand impulse that rewrites slack. NZ rates are unavailable, so the seat cannot show the cheap NZD is inconsistent with the NZ policy path. US gauges remain 69-75 after a delivered hike; that is not a risk-on USD-down regime.

cross-merchant short AUDNZD / NZD higher uses the 5y AUDNZD extreme as if NZ is the strong leg. The 16 Sep tape is AU housing contraction plus an NZ slowdown-that-beat. Inflation gauges are both hot (AU 82, NZ 80) while NZ labor is 32. Bidding NZD in the cross needs NZ rates or a growth-state change the packet does not mark.

rate-hawk and trend-follower pay SOFR_2027-09 on US heat 72/75/69/74 and a 90.5bp remaining SR3 path. That US-rates-up view is compatible with this seat. Their CA_RATES_UP / CAD_DOWN package is not: importing the Fed waypoint into a 122bp BoC cycle is the policy-error price CRAU27 already embeds. US restriction can persist without Canada delivering catch-up.

rate-dove receives CORRA_2027-06 on the same labor/core versus hike-path gap, then claims carry supports the trade. Fading a path that still prices 107.5bp to Jun-27 and 136.5bp to 2028-09 has negative path carry if those hikes print. Direction agrees; the carry claim does not.

mean-reverter's AONIA_2026-10 fade is not the USD/CAD/NZD opposite. The hole is only that AU inflation 82 still fights a 21bp October receive, which is why this seat would not have chosen AONIA as the primary slowdown expression.

events.rationale: Original trade stands: long duration CORRA_2027-09 / CRAU27. The discrepancy lives in the CAD policy path, not in USDCAD, NZDUSD, AUDNZD, or CA-US_2Y. Packet P&L on rates is inverted, so long duration profits if implied CORRA falls from 3.51. That is unchanged.; USD higher / CAD lower / NZD lower remain directional implications, not the risk. Transmission was already specified as fewer delivered CA hikes, not a required CAD crash. Energy can mix CAD spot; that is why spot was the inferior candidate. FX-view conflicts do not move the rates expression.; What would concede: CRAU27 implied through the packet 2028 peak of 3.655, or CA labor/activity re-accelerating with core well above 2%, or energy pass-through becoming a generalized CPI impulse that the BoC explicitly hikes into. A 4th-percentile CA-US_2Y print, a 0.2% NZ GDP beat, or hotter US gauges alone would not.; Uncertainty preserved: CFTC/CME missing; CORRA OI/volume null; gauges dashboard_v8; CA activity 66 is not recessionary; US heat can import some CA tightening. Confidence stays 58. Seat does not rank opponents or assert a house view.
